processing_steps.method: vacuum arc melting with remelting 5-6 times
processing_steps.atmosphere: 10^-5 mbar pressure, backfilled with argon gas
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Differential melting points of elements addressed by remelting ingot 5-6 times inside arc melter (AM500-Edmund Buhler GmbH, Germany) without breaking vacuum.
Nine passes in a 75-ton rolling mill; finish rolling temperature 900 °C.
Standard-route CR sheet annealed at 900 °C for 30 min followed by water quenching; this is the defining step producing sample A30.

structures.overall_structure: γ austenite matrix retaining three B2 morphologies after 30 min annealing: B2 stringer bands, needle-shaped intragranular IG-B2 (coarsened), and coarse intergranular GB-B2; URE-γ pancake structure persists and annealing twins nucleated in γ grains.

unmapped_findings: Ashby–Orowan precipitation strengthening calculation (Eq. 1): σ_IG-B2 = (0.538 G b √f_IG-B2 / D_IG-B2) ln(D_IG-B2 / 2b), with shear modulus G = 70 GPa and Burgers vector of γ b = 0.26 nm. For RE-γ: D_IG-B2 = 0.29 μm, f_IG-B2 = 1.1% → 23 MPa; for URE-γ: D_IG-B2 = 0.2 μm, f_IG-B2 = 2.6% → 43 MPa; total IG-B2 precipitation strengthening = 66 MPa. Note: these measurements are based on Figure 3a (A5); the paper states that longer annealing coarsens IG-B2 and reduces f_IG-B2, so A30's precipitation strengthening is lower than 66 MPa.

The paper also reports a modified (high-speed hot rolling, 10 rpm vs 1 rpm) route whose A30 achieves 1 GPa YS, best ductility, and toughness 1.72 kJ mol-1 (238 J cm-3). That A30 belongs to a different process (modified HR/CR route), not this standard-route proc_ann-900c-30min A30.

The standard-route A30 (Figure 5a) shows the lowest flow stress and largest strain among annealed samples but is part of an 'unsatisfactory stress-strain response' set that motivated the modified processing route.
